Effective communication is respectful exchange of ideas, not the will to win.

questions.stem: Air assets belonging to the AFP capable to provide close air support, maritime air patrol, disaster and rescue operations, evacuation, resupply and troop insertion.
questions.explanation: Aircraft are the AFP air assets that provide close air support, maritime air patrol, disaster rescue, evacuation, resupply and troop insertion.
why: Naval vessels are sea assets, not air assets.
Armored vehicles are ground combat assets.
Artillery pieces are ground fire support weapons.

questions.stem: It is a task that is crucial to the successful accomplishment of the mission.
questions.explanation: An essential task is crucial to the success of the mission; it always appears in the mission statement.
why: A constraint limits freedom of action and is not a task.
A supporting task helps another unit's task and is not by itself crucial to the mission.
A routine task is ordinary work not crucial to mission success.

questions.stem: Derived from the exploitation of imagery collected by visual photography, videos, multi-spectral sensors and radars.
questions.explanation: IMINT is derived from exploiting imagery gathered by photography, video, multi-spectral sensors and radar.
why: SIGINT is from intercepted emissions.
HUMINT is from human sources.
OSINT is from publicly available information.

questions.stem: You are the signal officer tasked with ensuring smooth communication support for an upcoming battalion operation. Before drafting the communication plan, you systematically examine terrain, enemy capabilities, available equipment, and troop movements. What step are you performing?
questions.explanation: The signal estimate is the systematic examination of terrain, enemy capabilities, equipment and troop movements before the signal plan is drafted.
why: Drafting Annex H comes after the estimate, using its conclusions.
Issuing the CEOI is done after planning is complete.
A communications rehearsal tests the plan afterward, not analyzes factors before it.

questions.stem: It will lead you to apply not only leadership, but also management and command and apply these to authority.
questions.explanation: Commandership combines leadership, management and command applied to authority. The commander practices the art of command.
why: Followership is the role of subordinates.
Mentorship is guiding juniors.
Stewardship is caring for resources or the profession.

questions.stem: What is an organization of stations capable of direct communications on a common frequency for a specific purpose?
questions.explanation: A radio net is an organization of stations capable of direct communications on a common frequency for a specific purpose.
why: An agency of communications is a facility with personnel and equipment.
A means of communications is the medium that carries a message.
A signal is the method of conveying information.

questions.stem: Leadership style that focuses on the exchange of skills, knowledge, resources, or effort between leaders and their subordinates.
questions.explanation: Transactional leadership is an exchange of skills, knowledge, resources or effort between leader and subordinates.
why: Transformational leadership inspires beyond self-interest.
Laissez-faire leaders do not exchange; they stay hands-off.
Autocratic leaders issue directives without exchange.

questions.stem: During a joint force operation against a heavily fortified enemy position, commanders decide to employ artillery, infantry, armor, and aviation units in synchronized action. What approach are they applying to achieve overwhelming effects on the enemy?
questions.explanation: Combined arms operation synchronizes artillery, infantry, armor and aviation to achieve effects greater than each could alone.
why: Mission command is a command philosophy, not the integrated use of different arms.
Warfighting functions are groups of tasks and systems.
Troop leading procedure is a planning process for leaders.

questions.stem: Which method can be used during an attack to transmit pre-arranged messages in accordance with CEOI?
questions.explanation: Visual and sound signals send pre-arranged messages per the CEOI during an attack when wire or radio is not practical.
why: Wire needs laid lines and is impractical in a moving attack.
A telephone switchboard needs wire infrastructure.
A data network is not suited to forward attacking elements.

questions.stem: Which principle of planning emphasizes flexibility and adaptability?
questions.explanation: Resilience is the planning principle stressing flexibility and adaptability, bouncing back and adjusting when conditions change.
why: Security protects information and systems.
Interoperability means units can communicate with each other.
Simplicity reduces complexity of plans.

questions.stem: What is the rated range of VHF radio for planning purposes?
questions.explanation: For planning, VHF radio is rated at about 10 kilometers because it is a line-of-sight system.
why: 5 kms is below the rated planning range for VHF.
20 kms is above the rated planning range.
40 kms is more than the planning range and fits high-throughput LOS radios.

questions.stem: What type of modulation limits the range due to line-of-sight operations (no obstacles exist between two stations)?
questions.explanation: FM, used on VHF, is limited to line of sight, so range depends on there being no terrain obstacles between stations.
why: AM is not the modulation tied to VHF line-of-sight combat net radio.
SSB is an HF mode used for longer ranges.
CW (Morse) is an HF mode, not tied to line of sight.

questions.stem: A considerate communication that equally valued and respected students for their ideas, beliefs, and values.
questions.explanation: Effective communication is respectful exchange in which ideas, beliefs and values of all are valued equally.
why: Innovation is introducing something new.
Warrior ethos is the will to win.
Doctrine is the authoritative guide on how the Army fights.

questions.stem: What characteristic must signal support have to be sufficiently mobile and adaptable to all possible battlefield conditions to support C2?
questions.explanation: Versatility means signal support is mobile and adaptable enough to meet all battlefield conditions to support C2.
why: Continuity is uninterrupted availability of information paths.
Security protects information from compromise.
Interoperability is ability to communicate across units and services.

questions.stem: During an intelligence operation, a unit collects information by intercepting enemy radar signals and voice communications over radio. What type of intelligence collection method is being used?
questions.explanation: Intercepting enemy radar signals and radio voice communications is SIGINT, with COMINT and ELINT as its parts.
why: IMINT uses imagery, not intercepted emissions.
HUMINT uses human sources.
OSINT uses public information.

questions.stem: It is an effect of fires delivered in a tactical mission task that physically renders an enemy force combat-ineffective until it is reconstituted and producing at least 30-percent casualties or materiel damage.
questions.explanation: Destroy physically renders an enemy force combat-ineffective until reconstituted, with at least 30-percent casualties or materiel damage.
why: Neutralize is only about 10-percent casualties or damage.
Suppress is only about 3-percent and is temporary.
Disrupt breaks up the enemy's formation and tempo and has no 30-percent measure.

questions.stem: Which planning process is used at battalion/brigade level?
questions.explanation: MDMP is used at battalion and brigade level, where a staff is available. TLP is for small units.
why: TLP is used by small-unit leaders at platoon and company level.
A signal estimate is a specific staff product, not the planning process.
A running estimate is an updated assessment inside the process.

questions.stem: In planning an armored assault, what key component helps coordinate movements with artillery and infantry units?
questions.explanation: Synchronization is arranging activities in time and space so the armor assault, artillery and infantry act together at the right moment.
why: Mission command is a command philosophy.
Doctrine is the authoritative guide, not coordination.
Command responsibility is accountability.

questions.stem: A leadership style where a leader works with teams/followers beyond their immediate self-interests to identify needed change, creating a vision to guide the change through influence, inspiration, and executing the change in tandem with committed members of a group.
questions.explanation: Transformational leadership works beyond self-interest to identify change, create a vision and execute it with committed followers.
why: Transactional leadership is exchange.
Laissez-faire leadership is hands-off.
Autocratic leadership is directive.

questions.stem: Refers to collective or organizational accountability and includes how well the unit performs its missions.
questions.explanation: Command responsibility is collective or organizational accountability, including how well the unit performs its missions.
why: Command is the authority exercised by rank or designation.
Ethical leadership is leading with sound moral standards.
Warrior ethos is determination and will to win.

questions.stem: What is a means of transmitting information in accordance with a certain pre-arranged system or code when direct verbal or written statements are unnecessary or impractical.
questions.explanation: A signal transmits information according to a pre-arranged system or code when direct verbal or written statements are unnecessary or impractical.
why: A radio net is stations on a common frequency.
An agency of communications is a facility with personnel and equipment.
Wires and cables are a physical means to interconnect nearby stations.

questions.stem: The authority that a commander in the armed forces lawfully exercises over subordinates BY VIRTUE OF RANK OR DESIGNATION.
questions.explanation: Command is the authority a commander lawfully exercises over subordinates by virtue of rank or assignment.
why: Command responsibility is accountability for unit performance.
Control is regulation of forces and functions, not the authority from rank.
Mission command is a philosophy of exercising command.

questions.stem: This shall be used by AFP units to determine the legitimacy of stations operating in the Net.
questions.explanation: Authentication is used by AFP units to verify that stations in a net are legitimate.
why: Encryption protects content, not station identity.
Frequency hopping resists jamming.
A radio check only tests signal quality.
